bib.title: ALBERT: A Lite BERT for Self-supervised Learning of Language Representations

question: Can parameter-reduction techniques and a coherence-based pretraining loss let BERT-style models scale to larger hidden sizes with fewer parameters and better downstream performance?
hypothesis: Untying embedding size from hidden size and sharing parameters across layers improves parameter efficiency, and sentence-order prediction is a more useful inter-sentence loss than next-sentence prediction.
contributions: New state of the art on GLUE, SQuAD and RACE with fewer parameters than BERT-large

method.summary: ALBERT is a BERT-style transformer encoder with factorized embeddings (V x E + E x H), all-layer parameter sharing, and an SOP loss added to MLM with n-gram masking. Models are pretrained on BooksCorpus and Wikipedia (plus extra data for final results) and fine-tuned on GLUE, SQuAD and RACE; ablations isolate each design choice.
method.task: self-supervised pretraining of language representations (MLM + SOP), then fine-tuning for NLU

limits: ALBERT-xxlarge is more computationally expensive than BERT-large (about 3x slower per step); authors name faster training and inference as next step (Sec 5).
Authors concede dropout finding may not hold for other transformer architectures; further experimentation needed.
Warm-start depth technique does not improve downstream performance (Appendix footnote).
Ablations use 125k steps and ALBERT-base; the largest models are not ablated.
Embeddings oscillate rather than converge across layers, unlike DEQ.
No wall-clock/FLOP accounting beyond relative speedups; no seeds or variance reported for ablations; random seeds not stated.
Evaluated only on NLU benchmarks (GLUE, SQuAD, RACE); superseded by later models (inferred).
